description: Per-character and per-shikigami ground/air movement tuning: run speed and turning, inertial/lean animation, target and camera-relative slowdowns, guard/landing inertia and landing rigidity.

Id.simple: Row key naming a movement profile (usually a character code; CP_210_2 is a CP_210 variant).
Id.technical: FName `Id` (exported as ID; DataTable ImportKeyField is Id). AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows first resolves the Action row (honouring a non-None ActionIdOverride), then finds ActionMoveDataTables by Action.Id_ActionMove and caches the pointer in AGameCharacter.ActionMoveRow; a miss fails character setup. Shikigami resolves Shikigami.Id_ActionMove through the same manager array; CP_210 also hard-codes CP_210_2. The struct has no explicit constructor store for Id (FName default None); all 50 exported rows have ID equal to their row key.

Foreground_Angle.simple: Angular cone for movement against the camera view that triggers slowdown.
Foreground_Angle.technical: Degrees; the half-angle is taken around straight-back. Character GetMoveSpeed enters the cone only when bForegroundSlow is true and this value > 0, then tests 180 - Angle/2 <= GameAnimNotify_AngleDegrees2D(view-forward, move-direction). Shikigami GetMoveSpeed applies the same cone test to its own row. C++ default 0.0f (off); all 50 exported rows are 180.

Foreground_Speed_Rate.simple: Speed multiplier at the centre of the foreground slowdown cone.
Foreground_Speed_Rate.technical: Speed factor at the exact centre of the slowdown cone: Factor = (180-angle)/(Angle/2) * (1 - Rate) + Rate, clamped to [0,1] and multiplied into speed; at the cone edge the factor is 1. C++ default 0.0f; 49 exports use 1.0 (no slowdown), CP_180 uses 0.7. The character and shikigami GetMoveSpeed helpers both read this field.

Target_Speed_Distance.simple: Distance within which movement near the target is slowed.
Target_Speed_Distance.technical: World units: character GetMoveSpeed measures 2D distance from controller Location3F0 to the target's GAISlot014 location and, when bTargetSlow is true, a valid target is within this distance, computes Distance / this value. There is no zero guard before the division; all 50 exports are 1500. C++ default 0.0f. The shikigami controller does not use this field; its target slowdown is a separate squared-distance curve.

Target_Speed_Rate.simple: Speed multiplier at zero distance from the target.
Target_Speed_Rate.technical: Speed multiplier at zero distance in the character target slowdown: Factor = distance/Target_Speed_Distance * (1 - Rate) + Rate, clamped to [0,1] and multiplied into speed; at the boundary the factor is 1. C++ default 0.0f; all 50 exports use 0.8. Not read by the shikigami controller.

ParallelAttack_Speed_Rate.simple: Speed multiplier while a parallel attack action is active.
ParallelAttack_Speed_Rate.technical: When Owner.IsAttackActionFlag15A() is true, character GetMoveSpeed multiplies speed by this field (no clamp) before the owner's GetMoveSpeedRate multiplier. C++ default 0.0f; 47 exports use 1.0, CP_070 and CP_210_2 use 0.8, CP_140 uses 0.6. Not read by the shikigami controller.

Run_Rotation_Time.simple: Time window over which the run turn is completed.
Run_Rotation_Time.technical: Seconds. FGameCharacterAction_RunBegin::Start copies it to RotationTimer; Tick decrements that timer and finishes the phase when the stick is released or the timer expires, and UpdateRequests requests GetDefaultMoveActionType() while the timer is positive, otherwise Run. Movement controller TickModeRunBegin separately sets RunTurnDuration61C = this value - MovePhaseElapsed and eases yaw over the remaining time. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.175 (43 of 50 use that value).

Run_Speed_Start.simple: Initial run speed when starting a run move phase.
Run_Speed_Start.technical: Units/second. Character SETMOVE_START_RUN uses this value unscaled as the FloatInterp28 start (only the end is scaled by GetRunSpeedRate()); shikigami mode 1 uses both start and end unscaled. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 750 and exported rows range from 150 to 850.

Run_Speed_End.simple: Target run speed at the end of the interpolation.
Run_Speed_End.technical: Units/second. Character SETMOVE_START_RUN passes GetRunSpeedRate() * this value as the interpolation end; shikigami mode 1 passes the raw field. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 800 and exported rows range from 450 to 900.

Run_InterpolateTime.technical: Seconds passed as the duration to FloatInterp28.Start when a run mode begins. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 and exported rows range from 0.25 to 1.0.

Run_EasingType.simple: Easing function for run speed interpolation.
Run_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType (uint8). ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc maps EaseIn/EaseOut/EaseInOut directly and sends every other value, including None and Invalid=255, to EEasingFunc::EaseOut. C++ default EGameEasingType::None; all 50 exports are None, so the shipped rows actually use EaseOut rather than a no-easing mode.

Run_Blend_Exp.simple: Exponent/shape parameter for run speed interpolation.
Run_Blend_Exp.technical: Float passed as the BlendExp argument to FloatInterp28.Start alongside Run_EasingType. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 2.0 (49 rows), CP_180 exports 1.0.

Run_Rotation_Rate.simple: Per-step rotation blend rate when turning toward input.
Run_Rotation_Rate.technical: Used in the run and target-run ticks when bSteerTowardMoveInput is set: 0 assigns the desired rotation directly, otherwise the controller calls GameVirtualCamera_LerpRotator with Rate * 60.000004 * Step. C++ default 0.0f (snap); CP_010 exports 0.2 (45 of 50 use that value) and exported rows range from 0.05 to 0.2.

Run_Inertia_Rate.simple: Inertia rate inherited when the previous action was Run.
Run_Inertia_Rate.technical: Applied when a new action inherits inertia from a previous Run action: character ApplyPrevInertia calls SetInertia and BlendInertiaFromAction calls BlendInertia; shikigami ApplyPrevInertia calls SetInertia. The (Rate, Time) SetInertia overload uses this rate for both XY and Z and resets inertia when rate <= 0 or time <= 0. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 and exported rows range from 0.2 to 1.0.

Run_Inertia_Time.simple: Duration over which run inertia is applied.
Run_Inertia_Time.technical: Seconds passed as the duration to SetInertia/BlendInertia in the Run previous-action arms. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (49 rows) and CP_180 exports 1.0.

Run_Lean_Rate.simple: Rate used to blend character lean while running.
Run_Lean_Rate.technical: Passed to the shared UpdateLeanRate: 0 snaps to the target lean, otherwise it interpolates with Rate * 60.000004 * Step. CP_240 instead reads the shikigami's MoveRow, assigns the target directly when this rate is 0, and uses Rate * 60.000004 as a per-frame lerp factor otherwise. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.3 and exported rows range from 0.2 to 0.4.

Run_Lean_Max.simple: Clamp for character lean while running.
Run_Lean_Max.technical: Maximum magnitude passed to UpdateLeanRate, which clamps the signed angle/45 target to [0, Max]; CP_240 also clamps shikigami LeanLR/LeanUD against the shikigami row's value. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 and exported rows range from 0.1 to 1.0.

Guard_Inertia_Rate.technical: XY rate passed to ScaleInertia when ground guard starts; ScaleInertia only restarts an already-active XY inertia interpolator. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (48 rows), CP_050 and CP_180 export 0.1.

Guard_Inertia_RateZ.technical: Z rate passed as the second ScaleInertia argument when ground guard starts; inactive Z inertia is unaffected. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (48 rows), CP_050 and CP_180 export 0.1.

GuardAir_Inertia_Rate.technical: XY rate passed to ScaleInertia by both the base GuardAir action and CP_180's override. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.3 (48 rows), CP_050 and CP_180 export 0.1.

GuardAir_Inertia_RateZ.technical: Z rate passed as the second ScaleInertia argument in air guard (also used by CP_180). C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (48 rows), CP_050 and CP_180 export 0.1.

GuardAir_Speed_Start.simple: Initial speed of the air-guard speed interpolation.
GuardAir_Speed_Start.technical: Units/second used as the FloatInterp28 start in SetMoveMode case 13 (air-guard movement); no owner rate multiplier is applied at this site. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 10.0 (48 rows), CP_050 exports 300.0 and CP_060 exports 50.0.

GuardAir_Speed_End.simple: Final speed of the air-guard speed interpolation.
GuardAir_Speed_End.technical: Units/second passed as the FloatInterp28 end in air-guard movement setup. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 2000.0 (49 rows), CP_050 exports 0.0, which makes the interpolation descend from its 300.0 start.

GuardAir_InterpolateTime.simple: Duration of the air-guard speed interpolation.
GuardAir_InterpolateTime.technical: Seconds passed as the FloatInterp28 duration in air-guard movement setup. C++ default 0.0f; all 50 exported rows use 0.5.

GuardAir_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType (uint8) converted by ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc; None and Invalid=255 both fall through to EEasingFunc::EaseOut. C++ default EGameEasingType::None; all 50 exported rows are None, so the effective easing is EaseOut.

GuardAir_Blend_Exp.technical: Float passed as the BlendExp argument to FloatInterp28.Start in air-guard movement setup. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (49 rows), CP_050 exports 2.0.

Landing_Inertia_Rate.technical: XY rate passed to ScaleInertia in FGameCharacterAction_LandingBase::Start. That site reads AGameCharacter::GetActionMoveRow() (the stored ActionMoveRow) directly, not GetCurrentActionMoveRow(), so the CP_210 row override does not affect landing inertia. C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.3, CP_040 and CP_210 export 0.1, CP_180 exports 1.0.

Landing_Inertia_RateZ.simple: Vertical inertia multiplier applied on landing.
Landing_Inertia_RateZ.technical: Z rate passed as the second ScaleInertia argument on landing, from the stored character ActionMoveRow (not the current/override row). C++ default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 0.5 (49 rows), CP_180 exports 1.0.

Rigidity_Landing.simple: Rigidity class used to scale landing hit/stun duration.
Rigidity_Landing.technical: EGameActionRigidityType (uint8: None=0, Light=1, Normal=2, Heavy=3, Invalid=255). GetLandingRigidityRate converts the enum to index uint8(Type) - 1 and reads GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_Landing; the exported Default array is [1.1, 1.0, 0.9], so all 50 rows (Normal) resolve to 1.0. None/Invalid or an out-of-range index/short array falls back to 1.0. The returned rate is passed as PlayAnimation's rate in the landing action. C++ default EGameActionRigidityType::None; all 50 exports are Normal.

notes: One exported table with 50 rows and no shards or locale variants. Every row serializes all 28 non-key fields; the struct has no in-header initializers and its constructor sets every numeric field to 0.0f, both easing enums to None and Rigidity_Landing to None. Exported rows override those defaults (notably Target_Speed_Distance=1500, Foreground_Angle=180 and Rigidity_Landing=Normal in all 50).

Row lookup uses the manager's ActionMoveDataTables array (registered from ActionMoveDataTable). Characters get the pointer from ActionDataTable.Id_ActionMove via ResolveDataRows and read it through GetCurrentActionMoveRow: the action controller's virtual row wins when a controller exists, including CP_210's cached CP_210_2 when bWeaponDrawn == 1 (its default); otherwise the stored ActionMoveRow is used. Landing inertia is the exception: it reads the stored row directly. Shikigami cache their own MoveRow from Shikigami.Id_ActionMove.

All 49 other exported rows are referenced by an ActionDataTable or ShikigamiDataTable Id_ActionMove join; CP_210_2 is the only row reached by a hard-coded lookup rather than a cross-table reference. A missing character row fails ResolveDataRows; a missing shikigami row returns false and keeps the previous pointer; the CP_210 hard-coded lookup has no fallback.

Foreground/Target slowdowns are conditional at the call site (bForegroundSlow/bTargetSlow); only the character GetMoveSpeed reads Target_Speed_Distance/Rate or ParallelAttack_Speed_Rate. Shikigami GetMoveSpeed reuses Foreground_Angle/Foreground_Speed_Rate but applies its own 3D follow-distance curve and its own speed-rate accessor.

None in EGameEasingType is not a no-easing value: ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc sends None (and Invalid) to EEasingFunc::EaseOut. All 50 rows export None for both easing fields, so the shipped speed interpolations use EaseOut.

Run_Speed_Start is unscaled; character Run_Speed_End is multiplied by GetRunSpeedRate(), while shikigami run speed uses both values unscaled. ScaleInertia fields only modify already-active inertia interpolators. Exported CP_010 values illustrate units but do not characterize every row (CP_050, CP_180, CP_210/CP_210_2 and several CN rows differ).
Evidence is from the locally reconstructed Abrams/AbramsDataTable C++; it is not a claim of retail byte-match, and no Blueprint or retail-runtime-only behavior is asserted.

usages.detail: Registers the loaded ActionMoveDataTable in the manager's ActionMoveDataTables array.
Resolves the required ActionMove row from ActionDataTable.Id_ActionMove into AGameCharacter.ActionMoveRow; a miss fails setup.
AGameCharacter::GetActionMoveRow exposes the cached stored row; the controller-aware sibling is GetCurrentActionMoveRow.
GetCurrentActionMoveRow prefers the action-controller virtual row when a controller exists, otherwise the stored row.
CP_210 caches a separate CP_210_2 row from the same manager array; slot 91 returns it while bWeaponDrawn == 1.
Character GetMoveSpeed applies target-distance, camera-relative and parallel-attack scaling from the row.
SETMOVE_START_RUN starts run speed interpolation from Run_Speed_* and easing fields.
RunBegin initializes RotationTimer from Run_Rotation_Time; line 701 uses the remaining timer to choose the next move action.
Uses Run_Rotation_Rate and lean fields while steering toward input.
Applies Run_Inertia_Rate/Time when the previous action was Run (SetInertia/BlendInertia variants).
Scales active inertia for ground guard.
Scales active inertia for air guard; CP_180 has an equivalent override site.
Scales inertia on landing from the stored ActionMoveRow (bypasses the current-row override).
Maps Rigidity_Landing through the 1-based rigidity index to GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_Landing.
Shikigami ResolveRows joins Shikigami.Id_ActionMove to the same table array and caches AGameShikigami.MoveRow.
Shikigami GetMoveSpeed reuses Foreground_Angle/Rate but not the character target-distance or parallel-attack fields.
Shikigami SetMoveMode starts run interpolation from its cached move row.
Shikigami inertia inheritance reads Run_Inertia_Rate/Time from the cached move row.
CP_240 reads shikigami Run_Lean_Max/Rate for its climb-turn lean animation.
Constructor establishes the 0/None defaults that differ from every shipped export.
